title: Shubh Detergents over the years
body: Shubh Detergents was set up when only a few firms made detergents and buyers bought whatever was available. The company produced at a large scale to keep its average cost and price low. As rivals entered, it improved its formula and added new features. When competition became intense, it hired a large sales team for door-to-door selling, backed by heavy advertising and discounts. Today the company first surveys households in its target market, has developed a powder suited to hard water at a price buyers are willing to pay, and has recently switched to biodegradable ingredients and refill packs to cut plastic waste, even though this raises its costs slightly.

title: Kiran Foods and its noodle campaign
body: Kiran Foods launched a new brand of instant noodles. Before its advertising campaign, it sold 5 lakh packs a year at a total cost of Rs 1 crore. It then spent heavily on a television and newspaper campaign. In the following year it sold 25 lakh packs, and its total cost, including the advertising expenditure, came to Rs 3.5 crore. A consumer group had earlier criticised the campaign, saying that advertising only adds to the cost of the product, which is passed on to buyers through higher prices.
